problem: exportProviderCatalogSnapshot swallows the snapshot write failure in an empty catch and then unconditionally returns { ok: true, path, summary }. The `ok` field is therefore always true and carries no information, and the JSDoc's promise (throws so a caller never believes it holds a snapshot it does not) is broken by the very next statement. Trigger: writeOwnerOnlyFileAtomic throws (destination directory missing, read-only path, disk full). Outcome: the caller (syncPinnedSnapshot -> loadOrRefreshWith) gets a success summary while no pinned file exists, so the later offline fallback silently finds nothing. Class scope: this is the only empty catch the change adds; the cache module's best-effort catches (removeProviderCatalogEntry etc.) carry a reason comment and return void, so they do not claim success.
impact: The operator on an air-gapped machine relies on a pinned snapshot that was never written; the failure is invisible at write time and only surfaces as a missing fallback later, far from its cause.

problem: The importProviderCatalogSnapshot JSDoc says a cache entry newer than the snapshot's copy is kept and only older or missing entries are replaced, but the loop calls updateProviderCatalogEntry, which overwrites the entry unconditionally (provider-catalog-cache.ts:234, `[entry.name]: entry`) with no fetchedAt comparison. The doc describes a merge rule no code path implements.
impact: A caller trusting the doc will import an old snapshot over a fresher live cache and lose newer entries; the next reader of this function is misled about its contract.

The pin/sync branches in loadOrRefreshWith and the summary helper are dead code with docs pointing at a nonexistent entry point.

problem: The catalog summary formula (sort names, count status === "ok", format "N provider(s), M live") is copy-pasted at three sites in this diff: provider-catalog-snapshot.ts:75-77 (export), provider-catalog-snapshot.ts:139-141 (import), and provider-catalog.ts:363-365 (formatCatalogSummaryLine). formatCatalogSummaryLine is the natural owner but the snapshot module re-implements it instead of calling a shared helper.
impact: Changing the wording or the 'live' definition (e.g. counting not-supported as connected) must be done in three places in two files; drift between the status line and the import/export summaries is likely.

problem: syncPinnedSnapshot takes a boolean flag `toPinned` that selects between two opposite operations (export cache -> pinned file, or import pinned file -> cache) with different failure semantics (export throws when no cache; import returns undefined when no file). Call sites read as `syncPinnedSnapshot(deps.dir, true)` / `syncPinnedSnapshot(deps.dir, false)`, which cannot be decoded without opening the signature. The import branch also reads the pinned file twice (readConfigFile at 154, then again inside importProviderCatalogSnapshot) and recomputes pinnedSnapshotFile(dir) three times.
impact: Callers must remember which boolean means which direction; the two directions cannot evolve their error handling independently. Two named functions (pinCatalogSnapshot / restoreFromPinnedSnapshot) would remove the flag.

problem: importProviderCatalogSnapshot is ~57 lines and mixes four responsibilities at different abstraction levels: file read and JSON parse, envelope validation (object/version/catalog/providers), per-entry filtering (sanitize, name match, maxAge), and persistence (per-entry cache writes plus prune), then summary formatting. Parsing/validating the snapshot envelope is a pure step that could be its own function (e.g. parseProviderCatalogSnapshot) separate from the merge.
impact: The validation cannot be tested or reused without touching disk, and each new option (prune, maxAge) grows the same function.

problem: Log-and-rethrow: the JSON.parse catch writes a message to stderr and then rethrows the raw SyntaxError, so the error that propagates carries no snapshot path/context while the context goes only to stderr. Every other failure in this function throws a contextual `provider catalog snapshot: ...` Error instead. The catch also binds `e` untyped.
impact: Callers that catch and report the error see a bare JSON SyntaxError, and the message is double-reported when a caller also logs; inconsistent with the sibling throws in the same function.

problem: Inconsistent error-handling posture: every cache writer in provider-catalog-cache.ts is best-effort and never throws (a cache is 'a courtesy, never a dependency'), but loadOrRefreshWith now awaits syncPinnedSnapshot, whose export branch throws when the cache is absent (e.g. after the best-effort saveProviderCatalogCache silently failed) and whose import branch throws on a malformed or wrong-version pinned file. Neither call is guarded, so a pinned-snapshot problem turns a successful refresh into a rejected one. Currently unreachable because nothing sets pinSnapshot (see G3).
impact: Once the pin option is wired up, a hand-edited or stale pinned file breaks catalog loading for every picker that calls loadOrRefresh*, contrary to the module's documented best-effort contract.

impact: Small misdirection for anyone looking for the file on disk.
